doc.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020

title: Giving up playing: jazz group and musical theater pit work
summary: He explains his jazz group ended after fifteen years and that he later enjoyed musical theater pit playing, which has now faded.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well I want to thank you for your career. I mean I consult the Grove a lot and I love books, so it’s a win-win. And it was quite a labor of love I think for you and well worth doing, in addition to all the other things you’ve done. I saw one picture on your website of you with a clarinet. I think you were on “Fiddler on the Roof.” Do you still play your instruments?

No that all sort of evaporated simply a period of life kind of things. We had a wonderful jazz group for almost fifteen years and I consider that a blessing to have a group last that long. But eventually you know, in a college community people move away and when it got to the point where we no longer had a chordal instrument we just couldn’t keep going anymore. And similarly I discovered late in life that I was much more talented as a musical theater performer than as a jazz musician. It’s something I didn’t know but the ability to switch instruments quickly and to read really well and the experience of jazz was important because I could — I had such a good knowledge of the repertory and I could know how to play with people and hear when something happens and so when the singer dropped out a verse I could go right with her. You know, and everybody’d follow Kernfeld, he knows where he is. You know. But that was something late in life that I enjoyed a lot and I had, you know, six different instruments that I could play in the pit. But that fell apart too for various just reasons, it slowly evaporated over the years. Last
year I played two musicals for one week each and this year none. So it’s all done. Unfortunately. It was fun. It was fun while it lasted.
